name: AgentBoard: An Analytical Evaluation Board of Multi-turn LLM Agents
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced. The full paper documents search/click WebShop actions and 11 browser actions in WebArena, while the overall benchmark also covers non-web domains.
summary: Introduces AgentBoard, a multiturn agent evaluation framework with intermediate progress metrics and analysis tools. Its broader task suite includes WebShop and WebArena interactions with stepwise progress measurements.

name: WebSuite: Systematically Evaluating Why Web Agents Fail
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: WebSuite organizes browser operations into an action taxonomy and tests both isolated controls and complete workflows. Its diagnostic tasks attribute failures to specific actions, enabling comparison of text-based and multimodal web agents.

name: OSWorld-Human: Benchmarking the Efficiency of Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: OSWorld-Human adds human-determined trajectories to OSWorld to evaluate the efficiency of desktop computer-use agents. The study compares 16 agents and analyzes model-call latency, changes in step duration during task execution, and excess action steps.

name: FineState-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Fine-Grained State Control in GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: FineState-Bench evaluates fine-grained GUI perception and control across desktop, web, and mobile interfaces. Its Visual Diagnostic Assistant separates perception and localization contributions in controlled interaction experiments.

name: You Don't Know Until You Click:Automated GUI Testing for Production-Ready Software Evaluation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: RealDevWorld evaluates generated software repositories with 194 development tasks and AppEvalPilot, an agent judge that operates the resulting GUIs. The evaluation examines functional behavior, visual fidelity, and runtime responses to produce task-specific diagnostic feedback.

name: AgentSentinel: An End-to-End and Real-Time Security Defense Framework for Computer-Use Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced. The official full paper confirms GUI/desktop interaction alongside Bash and file tools. Its abstract and body enumerate attack categories differently; no category count is promoted into this annotation.
summary: Introduces AgentSentinel, which intercepts sensitive computer-agent operations and audits them using task context together with system traces. BadComputerUse evaluates this enforcement approach across attack scenarios involving tool and computer control.

name: Detecting Pipeline Failures through Fine-Grained Analysis of Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces a modular framework for identifying errors at intermediate stages of a web-agent pipeline. A SeeAct and Mind2Web case study examines weaknesses that are obscured by final task-success metrics.

name: ProBench: Benchmarking GUI Agents with Accurate Process Information
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract. Experiments and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: ProBench extends mobile GUI evaluation with tasks whose correctness depends on the interaction process as well as the final state. Its ProcessProvider supplies process information for assessing agent behavior and analyzing failure modes.

name: Computer-Use Agents as Judges for Generative User Interface
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract. Experiments and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: AUI-Gym evaluates generated websites by having computer-use agents attempt tasks whose executability is checked programmatically. A feedback dashboard condenses navigation histories into visual summaries that a coding agent can use to revise an interface.

name: MobiBench: Multi-Branch, Modular Benchmark for Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: MobiBench evaluates mobile GUI agents offline while allowing multiple valid action paths. It decomposes agent pipelines into modules to study component contributions, configurations, and performance bottlenecks.

name: CUAAudit: Meta-Evaluation of Vision-Language Models as Auditors of Autonomous Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: CUAAudit examines vision-language models that judge computer-use task completion from an instruction and final environment state. Across macOS, Windows and Linux benchmarks, it measures accuracy, confidence calibration and disagreement between auditors.

name: Plover: Steering GUI Agents through Plan-Centric Interaction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Plover exposes GUI-agent plans and replanning as persistent artifacts that users can inspect and edit during execution. Its planner–executor design supports localized correction through plan edits, language guidance and screenshot-grounded interventions, studied through failure repair and workflow scenarios.

name: Sidekick: Designing Communication for Effective Multitasking with Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces Sidekick, a communication interface that uses ambient status cues, multimodal action summaries, and visual and verbal explanations of reasoning to help people monitor computer-use agents. A user study examines progress awareness, error traceability, and multitasking across background and foreground interaction.

name: How Benchmarks Mis-Score Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Audits failure-scored computer-use trajectories to distinguish agent errors from broken tasks and evaluator false negatives. It organizes reliability issues across task construction, trajectory evidence, scoring, and reporting, then derives corresponding evaluation design practices.

name: CURA: Certified Runtime Alarms for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces CURA, a telemetry-based runtime monitor that turns computer-use trajectories into sequential failure alarms and can trigger mid-task oversight. Its certificate controls false alarms, while the study separately reports detection performance and limits of retrospective monitoring.

name: OSWorld-Pro: Process-based Evaluation for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Adds annotated intermediate subgoals to computer-use tasks and uses process-oriented evaluation to identify action and progress failures.

name: GUITAR: Structured Failure Diagnosis of GUI Agents via State Transitions
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces GUITAR, which groups visually different screens into functional states and analyzes agent failures over a state-transition graph. It uses the resulting bottlenecks to diagnose recurring mobile and web errors and evaluate targeted guidance.

name: Absorbed in Inertia: Activation Analysis for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Studies repetitive, unproductive actions in desktop agents through their internal activation states. It proposes Reset, Reroute, Restore, a context intervention that temporarily resets an agent’s trajectory and later restores it to help escape repeated ineffective behavior.

name: GUI-HARVEST: Self-Improving GUI Agents through Evidence-Driven Harness Evolution
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Improves GUI-agent execution code by analyzing action effects and repeated-task failures, then validating bounded changes with frozen model weights.

name: Auditing Web Agent Evaluation on WebArena-Lite: Human Review of Outcomes and Trajectories
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Audits WebArena-Lite outcomes and trajectories with human review to identify automatic-evaluator false negatives and the first consequential execution errors. It also studies explicit execution-state memory and procedural guidance, showing why final task scores can miss substantial differences in agent behavior.

name: WebFovea: When the Model Is Right but the Click Is Wrong -- Reliable Round Trips for Vision-Based Web Agents on Live Websites
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Describes WebFovea, a vision-based live-web agent whose execution loop checks action parsing, browser effects, feedback accuracy, and observation delivery. The report analyzes failures such as coordinate mismatches and silent control interactions and documents corresponding harness changes.
